newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil CSN still in talks with pension funds.
newsitem.headline: Brazil CSN still in talks with pension funds.

text.p: Brazilian steelmaker CSN is still in talks with a group of pension funds to finalize details on their participation in the CSN-led consortium which will bid in the privatization auction of state mining giant CVRD.
"Negotiations are still going on, but an agreement could be signed any time," said CSN spokesman Francisco Padilha.

The six pension funds -- Previ, Petros, Sistel, Fapes, Funcef, Funcesp -- have been coveted as partners by both consortia planning to bid for the 40-45 percent voting stake in CVRD. The mining company is being auctioned April 29 for a base price of 3 billion reais ($2.83 billion).
Together the pensions have a 10.85 percent voting stake in CVRD, which would give the CSN consortium a controlling position within CVRD if it wins the auction.
The other consortium planning to bid for the CVRD stake, Valecom, is led by Brazilian metal, cement and pulp group Votorantim and South Africa's Anglo-American Corp .

Padilha said CSN had not signed any final agreement yet with any companies interested in joining the consortium, but some were close to being definite candidates like Nations Bank, South Africa's Gencor and Opportunity Asset Management.
He said Gencor would probably take a small stake in the consortium of around 10 percent, while NationsBank was planning to enter with a large chunk of money of between $1.2 billion and $1.5 billion.
Opportunity Asset Management, an offshore investment fund for foreign investors, confirmed it was joining the CSN consortium.
Opportunity Director Luiz Orenstein said mainly U.S. companies invested in the fund and so far no Japanese investors had joined.
Japanese steel and trading companies are seen as strong contenders for CVRD given their interest in securing a vital natural resource for their huge steel industry.

A spokesman for the Valecom consortium said the group was in advanced talks with a number of Japanese companies, but he could not confirm widespread press reports that a group of 12 Japanese firms led by Nippon Steel would join Valecom. He said their could be more Japanese companies interested.

He said Valecom was also negotiating with Brazilian metal and metallurgical group Caemi and CVRD's employees, who can acquire 4.45 percent of CVRD voting stock under the privatization rules and plan to join whichever consortium wins after the auction.
Caemi is of interest because of its experience in iron ore mining, CVRD's core business, the spokesman said.
